relation: logical equivalence, not convertibility: the frozen helpers spell the second clause as at most one member through each vertex (X15), pairwise-disjoint distinct members (X14) or empty pairwise intersections (X180), the canonical says that two members sharing a vertex are equal; certified by Packing.foundations.matching.matching_at_most_oneP, matching_pairwise_disjointP and matching_setI_eq0P (X180's edge set fg_edges G is E(G) by Extremal.migration.matching.fg_edgesE)
summary: Batch C, family C1 (`matching`). Six name-matched definitions were compared (table below); only the compiled simple-graph edge-family subgroup is migrated: `x15_matching` (packing, with the X18 chain), `x14_matching` (misc) and `x180_matching` (extremal) now unfold to upstream `GraphTheory.connectivity.matching M`, keeping their names as transparent aliases for one migration cycle. Statement texts, doc blocks, manifest rows, leg states and documented discrepancies are unchanged (checked below).
| `Packing.conjectures.X15.x15_matching` | simple-graph edge family; at most one member through each vertex | migrated: alias of `matching`; `Packing.migration.matching.x15_matching_compat` |
| `GTMisc.conjectures.X14.x14_matching` | simple-graph edge family; pairwise-disjoint distinct members | migrated: alias of `matching`; `GTMisc.migration.matching.x14_matching_compat` |

| `Extremal.conjectures.X180.x180_matching` | simple-graph edge family over `fg_edges G` (= `E(G)`, `fg_edgesE`); empty pairwise intersections | migrated: alias of `matching`; `Extremal.migration.matching.x180_matching_compat` |

| `Packing.conjectures.X15alone.x15_matching` | the X15 body, declaration for declaration (sha256 `e6463b96…`), in a self-contained file absent from `_CoqProject` | deferred, excluded: not built, not retargeted, not repaired; its documented stronger constant (c <= 32 (m+1)^3 under the corpus name) is preserved |

| `Hypergraph.conjectures.X6.x6_matching` | arbitrary hyperedge family on a finType (`M E : {set {set T}}`); identical body to `U12.hg_matching` (body sha256 `78f1f021…`) | deferred to the hypergraph foundation (batch D), together with `hg_matching` |

| `Digraph.conjectures.path_fas.matching` | predicate on a whole graph: a forest with every degree at most one | deferred, distinct representation: the bridge `matching G <-> connectivity.matching E(G)` needs its own comparison and a digraph build |

Nine statements are affected: five in X15 (corpus rows #02 and #03 and the three LLM-proof variants, which have no manifest row and are marked `non_corpus`), two in X18 (through `x18_perfect_matching`, a cross-file chain helper that reaches `x15_matching`), one in X14 and one in X180 (through `x180_induced_matching`, `x180_multitasker_capacity_at_least` and `x180_multitasker_capacity_positive`). Each frozen statement resolves only through frozen copies along its whole affected chain: every reference to a frozen name is `Legacy.`-qualified or prefix-stripped, so no frozen text contains a live name of the family. The per-row theorem `<formal_name>_compat : XnnLegacy.<formal_name> <-> <formal_name>` is kernel-checked by `meta/check_library_migration.py`.

Interaction with M1: the X15 and X14 chains reach the M1 aliases `x15_edge_set` and `x14_edge_set`. Their pre-M1 comprehension bodies are re-frozen as `Legacy.x15_edge_set` and `Legacy.x14_edge_set`, checked against 061154c (the same text M1 froze as `simple_edges.Legacy.edge_set` and `simple_edges.Legacy.exists_edge_set`), so every per-row certificate of X15, X18 and X14 is end-to-end over both migrations. X180 uses `GTBase.finite_graph.fg_edges`, which no migration redirected; `fg_edgesE` relates it to `E(G)`. The live helpers `x14_subcubic`, `x14_degree_two_count` and `x180_average_degree_logarithmic` reach no migrated name and are used as they are (`unchanged_live_helpers` records their hashes).

Preserved as documented: X15's REFUTED row #02 and PROVED row #03 (`foundations/fair_matching.v`), X18's partial row #01 (m = 2, 3 in the source) and X180's BLOCKED row (per-graph quantification of the capacity ratio and the degree constants, 2026-07-17 audit): the X180 certificate proves the frozen and the live statement equivalent, so that defect is neither repaired nor worsened. Perfect matchings, edge partitions and edge families stay separate families; they are frozen here only as chain dependencies.

Fidelity of the upstream-owned canonical: `meta/foundation_fidelity.json` enrols repository-declared primitives only, so the verdict is recorded in the registry (`matching.fidelity = FAITHFUL`, contract in `upstream_audit`) with the thirteen API and grounding theorems of `Packing.foundations.matching` as machine evidence (`Print Assumptions` clean, compiled by `check_library_migration.py`), and `packing-theory/theories/examples/matching.v` is the public downstream client (plan section 11). `digraph-theory/theories/conjectures/path_fas.v` appears among the canonical users below only because its deferred whole-graph predicate shares the short name `matching`. Kernel closure evidence (`Print All Dependencies` of every frozen and live statement) is kept separately under `coordination/evidence/C1-matching/`.
